In 2024, **12.8%** of Alberta children under 18 were in poverty. This uses the Market Basket Measure (2023 base), Canada's official poverty line. The estimate has "good" quality (grade C).

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, Table 11-10-0135-01, vector v1792632015 (Alberta, persons under 18 years, percentage in low income), reference year 2024.
- **Recent trend (same series):** 4.6% in 2020, 8.1% in 2021, 12.0% in 2022, 11.9% in 2023 and 12.8% in 2024. The 2020 and 2021 values are graded E, so use them with caution.
- **Older base year:** The 2018-base MBM (v1206133320) gives 11.7% for 2023. It ends at 2023 and has no 2024 value.
- **Other measures:** The table also has the after-tax Low Income Measure (LIM) and the low income cut-offs (LICO). I did not pull those figures, and they would give different rates.

In July 2026, the latest month available, average weekly earnings for all employees in Alberta's provincial and territorial public administration were **$1,877.58**, including overtime.

- **Trend:** Earnings rose from $1,667.49 in July 2025 to $1,877.58 in July 2026. That is about 12.6% higher. The monthly figures are unadjusted for seasonality, so some of the month-to-month movement may be seasonal.
- **Source:** Statistics Canada, Table 14-10-0203-01 (Average weekly earnings by industry, monthly), vector v1560358. The category is "Provincial and territorial public administration", which is the closest match to what you asked for. The series is rated "A" (the best quality grade).
- **Other measures:** The same table has a series excluding overtime (v1605659). It also has series for salaried and hourly-paid employees.
- **Annual figures:** Table 14-10-0204-01 has annual averages.
- **Hourly wages:** I only found hourly earnings for this industry in archived tables covering 1991–2000. I could not find current hourly figures.

The average total income of people aged 15 and over in Alberta was **$66,100** in 2024. That is in 2024 constant dollars and excludes people with zero income. The figure has a data quality rating of A (excellent).

- **Comparison:** The Canada-wide average for 2024 was $61,600 (v107660857).
- **Recent trend:** Alberta's average was $66,600 in 2020, $67,500 in 2021, $66,000 in 2022 and $66,300 in 2023. All are in 2024 constant dollars.
- **Source:** Statistics Canada, Table 11-10-0239-01 (Canadian Income Survey), vector v107680657, reference year 2024.

This is the average for individuals. Household or family income, and the median, are different figures. The median is usually lower than the average. I can pull those if you need them.

Alberta's median total income was **$96,600** in 2024, before tax and including government transfers. After tax it was **$85,300**. Both figures are in 2024 constant dollars, and both have a data-quality rating of A (excellent).

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, Table 11-10-0237-01, Canadian Income Survey, reference year 2024.
- **Vectors:** v107654786 for total income and v107654846 for after-tax income.
- **What the unit is:** The table counts economic families and persons not in an economic family. These are close to households but not identical. I found no table in this database that gives a median for households themselves.
- **Trend:** The 2023 median total income was $98,400, so the 2024 figure is slightly lower.
- **Census figure:** The 2021 Census has household income statistics for 2020 incomes in Table 98-10-0060-01. I did not pull that figure.

In 2024, the latest year available, **12.8% of Alberta children under 18 were in poverty**. This uses the Market Basket Measure (2023 base), Canada's official poverty line. The estimate has "C" (good) data quality.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, Table 11-10-0135-01, Canadian Income Survey, vector v1792632015, reference year 2024.
- **Other measure:** On the after-tax Low Income Measure, a relative measure, the 2024 rate was 13.9% (v96520326, quality C).
- **Trend:** The Market Basket Measure rate was 4.6% in 2020, 8.1% in 2021, 12.0% in 2022, 11.9% in 2023 and 12.8% in 2024.
- **Older base:** On the 2018-base Market Basket Measure, the 2023 rate was 11.7% (v1206133320). That series has no 2024 value.

The survey excludes people living on reserves.

Average weekly earnings for all employees in Alberta's provincial and territorial public administration, including overtime, are:

- **Latest month, July 2026:** $1,877.58 per week. This is Table 14-10-0203-01, vector v1560358, unadjusted for seasonality. It was $1,819.70 in January 2026.
- **Annual 2025:** $1,702.65 per week. This is Table 14-10-0204-01, vector v1742415. The earlier years were $1,666.95 in 2022, $1,703.25 in 2023 and $1,677.47 in 2024.

These are weekly earnings from Statistics Canada's Survey of Employment, Payrolls and Hours. The category is "provincial and territorial public administration", and the tables don't separate Alberta's provincial government from any territorial component. There are also versions that exclude overtime: v1605659 (monthly) and v1797937 (annual).

I didn't find a current Alberta hourly wage for this industry. The only hourly table I found, 14-10-0103-01, covers just 2016–2017.

In 2024, the average total income of Albertans (before tax, including government transfers) was **$63,200**. The figure is in 2024 constant dollars and covers all persons aged 15 and over. Statistics Canada rates its quality "A" (excellent).

|---|---|
| Market income (before taxes and transfers) | $55,900 |

Total income was $63,400 in 2022 and $63,900 in 2023, so it dipped slightly in 2024.

Source: Statistics Canada, Table 11-10-0091-01 (Canadian Income Survey), reference year 2024. Vectors: total income v1529672282, market income v1529672276, after-tax income v1529672288.
